title: Jeremiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 24
description: Ten questions on Jeremiah 24: the two baskets of figs before the temple and what Yahweh said each basket stood for.

questions.text: What did Yahweh show Jeremiah, set before Yahweh's temple?
questions.explanation: Yahweh showed him two baskets of figs that were set before Yahweh's temple.

answers.text: A boiling pot facing the north
Two baskets of figs
A basket of summer grain
A yoke of wood and bars of iron

questions.text: Which king of Judah had Nebuchadnezzar already carried away captive to Babylon before this vision?
questions.explanation: The vision came after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away captive Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, with the princes of Judah, the craftsmen and the smiths.

answers.text: Josiah
Zedekiah
Shallum
Jeconiah

questions.text: What were the figs in the first basket like?
questions.explanation: One basket had very good figs, like the figs that are first-ripe.

answers.text: Very good, like figs that are first-ripe
Dried and pressed into cakes
Small but still green
Mixed, some good and some bad

questions.text: What is said about the figs in the other basket?
questions.explanation: The other basket had very bad figs, which could not be eaten, they were so bad.

answers.text: They were sweeter than those in the first basket
They had all been eaten by the birds
They were so bad that they could not be eaten
They were still ripening on the branch

questions.text: When Yahweh asked Jeremiah what he saw, what did he answer?
questions.explanation: Yahweh asked, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" and he said, "Figs. The good figs are very good, and the bad are very bad, so bad that can't be eaten."

answers.text: An almond branch
Figs
Two baskets of bread
A field of grain

questions.text: Whom did Yahweh say He would regard like the good figs?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said that like the good figs He would regard the captives of Judah, whom He had sent out of that place into the land of the Chaldeans, for good.

answers.text: The priests who served in the temple
Those who stayed behind in Jerusalem
Those who had gone down to Egypt
The captives of Judah sent into the land of the Chaldeans

questions.text: What did Yahweh promise to do with them when He set His eyes on them for good?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said He would bring them again to this land, and would build them and not pull them down, plant them and not pluck them up.

answers.text: Build them and not pull them down, plant them and not pluck them up
Give them rule over all the nations around them
Keep them in the land of Babylon for ever
Make them like the baskets of first-ripe figs

questions.text: What did Yahweh say He would give them, so that they would return to Him with their whole heart?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said, "I will give them a heart to know me, that I am Yahweh," and that they would be his people and He would be their God.

answers.text: A new name
A book of his words
A heart to know Him
Shepherds to feed them

questions.text: Whom did Yahweh compare to the bad figs that could not be eaten?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said He would give up Zedekiah the king of Judah, his princes, the remnant of Jerusalem who remained in the land, and those who dwelt in the land of Egypt.

answers.text: Zedekiah, his princes, the remnant of Jerusalem and those in Egypt
The craftsmen and the smiths taken to Babylon
The kings of all the nations around Judah
Jeconiah and all the captives of Judah in Babylon

questions.text: What three things did Yahweh say He would send among them until they were consumed from the land?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said, "I will send the sword, the famine, and the pestilence, among them, until they are consumed from off the land that I gave to them and to their fathers."

answers.text: Darkness, hail and fire
Drought, locusts and flood
Wormwood, poisoned water and a storm
The sword, the famine and the pestilence
